messages.content: Calculate the slope gradient in degree between two points on a landscape with coordinates (40.7128, -74.0060) and (34.0522, -118.2437).

function.name: calculate_slope_gradient
function.description: Calculate the slope gradient between two geographical coordinates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

point1.description: The geographic coordinates for the first point [Latitude, Longitude].

point2.description: The geographic coordinates for the second point [Latitude, Longitude].

unit.description: The unit for the slope gradient. Default is 'degree'.

message.content:
I’m happy to help you work out the slope gradient!  
To determine an inclination (in degrees), we need **both**:

| What’s needed | Why it matters |
|-----------------|---------------|
| **Elevation at each location** – e.g., meters above sea level | Gives us the “rise” component of the slope |
| **Horizontal separation** – usually the ground‑distance along the surface (great‑circle distance for straight lines across Earth) | Provides the “run” component |

With only latitude/longitude pairs \((40.7128°, −74.0060°)\) and \((34.0522°, −118.2437°)\) we can compute how far apart those places sit horizontally (~\(3935\) km using haversine formula), but without their respective altitudes we cannot find the rise/run ratio—and therefore the slope angle—between them.

If you happen to know the elevations (or even just the relative height change) for either point, please share them and I’ll plug everything into the `calculate_slope_gradient` routine right away. If not, let me know what kind of estimate you’re after (e.g., assuming flat terrain, average regional relief, etc.) so we can decide on the best next step.
